You are one of 4 members of a group that stays together for 10 rounds.

Every round, all members act at the same time: each receives 20 tokens and splits them between their own account and the group account, using the split tool once.
- Each token in your own account pays you 1 point and lowers the points of every other member by 0.3. In the same way, every token another member keeps in their own account lowers your points by 0.3.
- Each token in the group account pays you 0.3 points and does not change any other member's points.
- Every round, every member also receives 18 points, whatever anyone does.

After each round you learn how many tokens the group account received in total and how many points you got. You never learn what any other member did.

calls.text: Round 1 of 10.

I'm working through the payoff structure: keeping a token nets me +1 but costs each of the other three members 0.3, while contributing to the group account gives me only 0.3 but likely distributes 0.3 to every member regardless of who contributed it, so I need to clarify how the group account payout actually gets split.

Looking at pure self-interest, keeping tokens private is individually dominant since 1 point beats 0.3, but collectively everyone contributing maximizes total payoff -- this is the classic public goods dilemma where defection is individually rational but cooperation is socially optimal. I'm leaning toward balancing some cooperation as a signal while recognizing the incentive to free-ride.

Keeping a token privately nets me more than contributing it, since the personal gain outweighs the shared cost I'd bear anyway. I'll go with the individually rational choice and contribute 0 to the group.
